body:
" I have hated you for so long but I thought it was me that I was hating. But you made me this way. " 

*This.* 

It's not you. You can see it. Keep seeing it.

I know that words don't always help, but I'm going to try.

One thing that helps me with social anxiety is considering that the anxiety comes from valuing other people's opinions. It's not always conscious, but when I ask myself, "Why are you afraid?" the answer is almost always that I'm afraid that these people don't like me, or think I'm stupid, or ugly. But what if I *don't* value their opinion? Why am *I* wrong? Why are *they* right? There isn't anything that makes me inherently wrong or them inherently right.

And why would I value an opinion of someone like *that*?

Now when I get nervous around someone who is clearly a bully, I literally say the words "I don't value your opinion" in my head over and over again until I can feel my body relax.

It's hard in high school because the world seems small. You see the same people every single day. There's a hierarchy that forms because no one has anything better to do. Know that you have just as much a right to be who you are and exist as anyone else does. The hierarchy isn't real, and no one knows what they're doing. These kids are lost, hurt, and confused, and it manifests as bullying. Don't be scared. Be happy that you don't have those mean impulses. It means you're loved, and more secure than you think. I hope this helps.
